_docked_throughout: DOCKED FOR THE WHOLE RUN, which is what makes this the cheapest scenario in the 18-20 set: it never launches, so the system populator that blocked oo-qwk5 and forced scenario 001 to dump the smallest possible world does not apply. `undocked_seen` is expected FALSE and is RECORDED as false in the dump rather than omitted, so a run that somehow launched fails by name.
_award_key: NAMED HERE, not picked as 'whatever was first in a list' - the catalogue's own requirement. A list-order pick would make the scenario silently measure a different item the day the registry is reordered, which is precisely the regression this scenario exists to catch. EQ_FUEL_SCOOPS is damageable (canBeDamaged true, measured) and not carry-multiple, so it can carry BOTH the OK->DAMAGED transition and the duplicate-award refusal.
_undamageable_key: The OTHER refusal arm. equipment.plist gives EQ_CARGO_BAY `damage_probability = 0`, and OOEquipmentType.m:556-568 therefore reports canBeDamaged FALSE. MEASURED on this build: setEquipmentStatus(EQ_CARGO_BAY,'EQUIPMENT_DAMAGED') returns false and the status stays EQUIPMENT_OK (OOJSShip.m:2920-2928 warns rather than damaging). A refusal is positive evidence the status machine applies rules.
_purchase_key: The item bought with credits. TL 2 <= the station's TL 4, so it is genuinely on sale here, and its price is a round 6000 in equipment.plist - read out of the ENGINE's loaded registry at run time, never out of the plist by this harness.
_above_tech_level_key: THE CONTROL THAT MAKES THE TECH LEVEL MEAN SOMETHING. One key on one side of a threshold passes against any constant, including a station reporting 0 or NSNotFound. EQ_DOCK_COMP is TL 9, above this station's 4, so the pair straddles the value and a degenerate tech level fails the two-sided predicate.
_expected_station_tech_level: Lave's Coriolis reports equivalentTechLevel 4, matching the system's own techlevel. PlayerEntity.m:9300-9308 prefers the STATION's value when it declares one, so both are stored and a divergence between them is visible rather than absorbed.
_expected_price_factor: StationEntity.m:696-697 reads `equipment_price_factor` from the station's shipdata and floors it at 0.5; Lave's main station declares none, so it is the 1.0 default. Pinned because it is one of the two multiplicands of every price this scenario records.
_credits_start: SETUP, NOT MEASUREMENT. The standard save carries 100 credits and the purchase costs 6000, so the balance is topped up to a pinned value first; what is MEASURED is that the engine's price and the station's factor produce the recorded delta. PlayerEntity stores credits as deci-credits (PlayerEntityScriptMethods.m:52-59), so the value must be representable to one decimal place - 20000 is.
_min_registry_entries: A floor on the enumerated equipment registry, under what this build loads (measured: the stock registry is far larger). It rejects a run where equipment.plist did not load at all: an order pinned over three entries cannot see the reordering item 0.1 names, so a short registry must refuse rather than compare.
_repopulator_handlers: oolite-populator.js's repopulate handler. Its station picker `_tradeStation` tests hasNPCTraffic inside its loop but ENDS WITH an unconditional `return system.mainStation`, so switching the flag off does not stop it launching. The name is pinned here so an upstream rename becomes a red rather than a silent no-op.
